newsitem.title: GERMANY: BA plans Q1 ex-Germany air cargo rate rise.
newsitem.headline: BA plans Q1 ex-Germany air cargo rate rise.

text.p: British Airways World Cargo said it will introduce some limited ex-Germany rates rises on January 1, ahead of a general increase towards the end of the first quarter.
Cargo manager Central Europe, Mark Gardiner, said the January rates increase was only a small increase affecting just one or two routes.
"Towards the end of the first quarter we will review our rates with a view to putting them up," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
But it was too early to say what levels of increases the airline might consider at that stage, he said.
"We are looking to push up some of these rates to bring them in line with other airlines. Once we improve service standards we can sell ourselves more aggressively," he added.
"There is a market need to up rates and an internal need to make them more attractive in terms of internal capacity planning," Gardiner said.
BA business in Germany was a little weak in December, possibly due to service shortfalls in the UK having cost the airline market share, he added.
"It does not seem to be a boom at present but we are seeing robust volumes on our core routes such as the North Atlantic," he said. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
